name: Austin Wingate

identification: Two men in frame. Three cues agree on the sharp foreground man at left: he is named first in a caption that runs left to right, he is the only one in focus and so the frame subject, and the caption has him doing the talking while he is the one mid-word. That this is the SGA Austin Wingate rather than a namesake is supported by the Herald of 20 March 2012 (Vol. 87 No. 29), which lists Austin Wingate as one of three candidates for SGA president, so he was a student until 2012 and a WKU graduate by 2017.

identification: One living person is in the frame; the two other figures the caption names are a cardboard cutout and a figurine. That this is the senator: the Herald of 10 February 2009 calls SGA senator Jacob Turner an 'Ary senior', and Ary is a Perry County community ten miles from Hazard, which is where this man's home is; the class year is the paper's own error, settled by SGA's minutes, which still have Jacob Turner taking over the Legislative Research chair in February 2010, a year after he was supposedly a graduating senior.

name: Dave Vickery
why: The only photograph of him in any WKU source. Eyes are lowered to the papers he is reading, but the face is lit, sharp and unobstructed. Cut from the 1719x1119 press photograph at the scan's native resolution.
caption_quote: Danville junior Kevin Smiley, Taylor Mill junior Dave Vickery and Lexington freshman Daniel Shaw
identification: Three men sit in a row on one sofa and the caption names three people. Smiley is named first, so the caption runs left to right, which puts Vickery, named second, in the centre and Shaw, named third, at the right. That this is the SGA man: the article on p. 4 of the same issue names 'Taylor Mill junior David Vickery' as the one Western student on the Frankfort trip who was not then in SGA, and the Herald of 30 April and 7 May 2009 has 'Taylor Mill sophomore David Vickery' writing and re-writing SGA's AARC funding bill; he chaired Academic Affairs the following year. name: Hannah Garland
why: Her own studio portrait from the university yearbook, taken in the year she was Director of Academic and Student Affairs: front on, evenly lit, eyes open, smiling. Extracted at the printed image's native resolution, 434x579; not upscaled. NOTE FOR THE EDITOR: years.json also carries her as a senator in 2011-12, and this portrait would serve that record equally.
caption_quote: Hannah Garland
identification: The underclassmen grid prints four portraits to a row with the row's four names set beside it in a single column, top to bottom matching left to right. Garland is the fourth name of the second row on p. 299, so hers is the fourth and rightmost portrait, at x 1087-1191. The mapping is checked, not assumed: on this spread the eight rows' name lists and portraits agree on sex in all thirty-two cases (row 2 reads Frazier, French, Gachassin, Garland against man, man, woman, woman), and both the names and the portraits run in strict alphabetical order, so a shift by one place anywhere would break both checks. That this is the SGA woman: the Herald of 2 April 2013 identifies its letter-writer as 'Hannah Garland ... chair of academic affairs and part of the Student Government Association', the same year and the same campus, and the Talisman grid holds one Hannah Garland.

name: Roy Ratliff
why: His own studio senior portrait from the university yearbook, at full printed resolution: front on, evenly lit, eyes open, smiling, shirt and tie. The best frame of anyone in this block.
caption_quote: Roy Ratliff / Chicago / Management
identification: The seniors grid prints three portraits to a row with that row's three names, each with hometown and major, set beside it in one column, top to bottom against left to right. Ratliff is the second of the three names against the second row on p. 283, so his is the middle portrait, at x 897-1043. The pairing is verified on the same spread: the row below reads Mark Reeves, Laura Rich, Brenda Roberts against a young man, a woman and an older woman, and the young man in the first position is wearing a black polo with SGA embroidered on the chest, which is Reeves, SGA's executive vice-presidential candidate that spring. Sexes agree in every row on the spread. That this is the senator at large of 2012-13: Ratliff is a rare surname, absent from the digitised Herald back file for these years, and a senior in the 2013-14 book was in the Senate the year before.

name: Ben Lineweaver
why: A posed head-and-shoulders portrait in jacket and WKU tie, front on, eyes open, smiling; the only photograph of him anywhere in the digitised archive. Extracted at the printed image's native resolution and not upscaled.
caption_quote: BENJAMIN LINEWEAVER
identification: SGA's own full-page election advertisement, printed p. 12 of the Herald of 9 April 2009 under the heading SGA SENATE RACE with the WKU Student Government Association logo. It is a one-name-one-face grid: three office rows down the left margin (President, Executive Vice President, Administrative Vice President) with each candidate's photograph and their name set immediately beside it in large type. Lineweaver's name sits directly to the right of this frame in the Executive Vice President row; measured off the page, the name block runs x 168-311 and the image rect x 173-303 on the row below it, and no other photograph is on that side of the row. Checked as the same man as the archive's 2008-09 Campus Improvements chair: he is standing for SGA executive office in the spring of his own year of service, and Lineweaver appears nowhere else in the Herald back file for these years except his relative Cherieth Lineweaver, the 2007 candidate.

name: Kat Johns
why: A front-on studio-style mugshot cut for the Herald's own vox pop column, evenly lit, eyes open, smiling. It is the only photograph of her in any WKU source. Small because that is the printed size; rendered at the embedded image's native resolution and not upscaled.
caption_quote: KAT JOHNS, Bowling Green sophomore
identification: The 'So who do you follow?' column on p. 12 of the Herald of 3 November 2009 runs three students down the left margin, each as one block: a mugshot at x 27-85 with the student's answer set beside it at x 99 and the student's name in bold at the foot of that answer. The three blocks do not overlap vertically. Johns's name sits at y 542, inside the band of the top photograph (y 481-571); the second photograph's band (y 579-669) carries Liz Floore's answer and name, the third (y 677-767) Danielle Tosti's. One photograph, one answer, one name, three times over. That this is the SGA senator: the whole digitised Herald back file holds exactly one Kat Johns, a Bowling Green freshman in February and March 2009 who chaired the academic affairs committee and co-wrote the study-abroad scholarship bill, and a Bowling Green sophomore here eight months later. Her answer names her sorority sisters, and the Kappa Delta new-member advertisement of 4 September 2009 lists Kat Johns.

name: Laura Harper
why: The only photograph of her in any WKU source. A group crop, front on, eyes open, smiling, evenly lit studio light. Cut at the printed image's native resolution and not upscaled, which is why it is small.
caption_quote: Row 2: Sarah Stout, Laura Harper, Brent Shinkle, Ebony Lee, Macy Lethco
identification: The 2015 Talisman's club section prints each group photograph with a numbered row key beside it. The Revolution 91.7 photograph on p. 328 is keyed Row 1: four names, Row 2: five names, Row 3: six names. The picture holds exactly four people in the front row, five in the middle and six at the back, so Row 1 is the front and the counts fix the rows before anything else is assumed. The sexes then confirm each row independently: Row 1 reads Taylor Hodgkins, Diamond Darling, Angela Conway, Ford Parson against three women and, last, one man; Row 2 reads Sarah Stout, Laura Harper, Brent Shinkle, Ebony Lee, Macy Lethco against woman, woman, man, woman, woman; Row 3 reads David Hormell, Jeris Johnson, Cameron Coats, Michael Bowlds, Madison Martin, Ben Potts against five men with the one woman fifth. All three rows line up, so Harper is the second face from the left of the middle row, the woman with red hair. That this is the SGA officer and not a namesake: the Herald calls her 'Louisville sophomore Laura Harper, an SGA senator-at-large' on 12 April 2013 and quotes her right through the autumn of 2013 as SGA's director of public relations, then on 20 November 2014 calls her 'Louisville senior Laura Harper, a director at Revolution'. Sophomore in spring 2013 is senior in autumn 2014, the same Louisville student, and Revolution 91.7 is the club in this photograph. The digitised Herald holds no second Laura Harper in these years.
